newsitem.title: CANADA: FOCUS-Canada's Hargrove slams government vote order.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Canada's Hargrove slams government vote order.

text.p: Canadian Auto Workers President Buzz Hargrove said on Wednesday that the federal labor minister's decision to force a vote on a restructuring plan to save Canadian Airlines Corp. violates workers' rights.
Hargrove told Reuters the order from Labor Minister Alfonso Gagliano instructing CAW members to vote on an offer from the embattled airline circumvented the bargaining process.
"This is a major intrusion into the rights of working people. The government has violated the rights of our members," Hargrove said in an interview.

Hargrove said he was uncertain whether the union, which represents about 3,700 of Canadian's 16,400 employees, would comply with the order. He said the bargaining committee for the airline employees would meet to decide whether it would hold a vote.
"The bargaining committee is going to make that decision," he said. "I don't know if there is going to be a vote yet."
Gagliano told parliament on Wednesday that he was invoking a little-used section in the Canadian Labor Code to force the vote, which has been adamantly opposed by Hargrove.
The CAW, alone among Canadian's six unions, had opposed the restructuring plan for Canadian Airlines, which includes wage cuts to save the airline C$35 million ($26 million) a year.

Canadian executives have said Canada's second biggest airline could cease operations early next year unless the plan was implemented. The Calgary, Alberta-based carrier has said all its unions must agree to the deal.
The plan includes federal and provincial government support and a C$48 million ($36 million) year cut in fees paid to 33 percent-owner AMR Corp., the parent of American Airlines.
Canadian also is trying to postpone about C$170 million ($125 million) in debt payments over the next six months from 70 creditors and equipment lessors, a move contingent on the plan being in place.
Gagliano's move came hours after a meeting of Hargrove, Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson and Canadian Chief Executive Kevin Benson broke up after 20 minutes without an agreement.

"We are at an impasse and 16,000 jobs are at stake here. So that's why I directed the Canada Labor Relations Board to organize a vote for the employees of Canadian Airlines who are members of the Canadian Automobile Workers union..." Gagliano told parliament.
Gagliano told reporters later he hoped the unprecedented vote on the deal would take place "in a matter of days."
But CAW leaders said a vote could take longer -- anywhere from a week to 10 days.

Labor experts said the government had interfered before in cases involving labor disputes. But they said Article 107 of the labor code invoked by Gagliano did not cover the situation with Canadian as it did not involve a threat to "industrial peace."
"I'd be surprised if this matter didn't end up in the courts," said Dan Oldfield, senior staff representative at the Canadian Media Guild.
Canadian was quick to applaud the government's move.
Earlier, in a somber message to employees recorded shortly after the meeting with Hargrove but before Ottawa's move, Benson voiced grave concern over the airline's future.
But Transport Minister Anderson ruled out any government bailout for the ailing company other than a fuel tax rebate he offered last week.
